newsitem.title: CANADA: CBRS confirms Canadian Pacific rating.
newsitem.headline: CBRS confirms Canadian Pacific rating.

text.p: Canadian Bond Rating Service said on Tuesday it confirmed Canadian Pacific Ltd's short- and long-term debt at A-1 (Low) and A (Low) following the announced sale of its Marathon Realty Co Ltd unit.
The bond rating agency said the ratings of securities issued by two Canadian Pacific units, Canadian Pacific Enterprises Ltd and Canadian Pacific Securities Ltd are currently under review.
The debentures and commercial paper of the two wholly-owned Canadian Pacific units are now rated at A and A-1 respectively.

CBRS said the confirmation of Canadian Pacific's ratings reflects the company's major presence in three sectors of the economy and financial flexibility enjoyed through determinable source of cash flow.
The agency said the sale of the Marathon unit will generate about C$952 million for Canadian Pacific which improves the consolidated debt leverage position of the conglomerate.
The sale of Marathon will remove about C$700 million of debt from Canadian Pacific's balance sheet and improve financial flexibility, CBRS said.

CBRS said it placed the ratings of the two Canadian Pacific units under review because the previously-held direct interests by Canadian Pacific Enterprises in Fording Coal, CP Hotels & Resorts and Canadian Pacific Securities have been transferred to other wholly-owned subsidiaries of Canadian Pacific.

CBRS said its credit review will determine whether there has been any change in credit risk attached to securities issued by Canadian Pacific Enterprises and Canadian Pacific Securities after the transfer of underlying assets.
